title: Lester Young replacing Coleman Hawkins in Henderson's sax section
summary: Procope was there when Lester joined; the band's sound suffered, Fletcher disliked it, and Ben Webster came in with a big Hawkins-like tone.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Let me just stop you there to ask you one thing. Were you with Fletcher when Lester Young replaced Coleman Hawkins?

Tell me about that before we go on. Because I remember I interviewed Lester and Lester told me that he had a terrible time because people kept saying they wanted to hear him play like Coleman Hawkins.

Well, I suppose that was only natural. But actually, the sound of Fletcher Henderson's band suffered, and with all bands that are popular, the band itself has a certain sound which has nothing to do with the calibre of musicians, let's put it that way, who are in the band, or who takes whose place or whatever. So Lester's sound when he came with the band, it left a big void, a big hole in the sound of the band which was no, you know, not casting any reflection on Lester, because he played, and there were some people who heard Lester with the band, they said, 'Yeah, he's tough, you know.' Like that. And I don't believe that Fletcher didn't like Lester's sound, and I --
Yes, because there were a lot of things involved. I think we came through Kansas City or something like that. Somebody recommended Lester, you know, as a tenor

player. But the thing about it is that Fletcher didn't like him at all. That's how Ben Webster got in the band, see, because -- then I remember when Ben joined the band, after Lester left, you know, then everybody agreed that Ben Webster had the big sound. And like I said before, he had the tone. Ben could play pretty and he had a tone which Coleman had and Lester didn't have.
When Lester left, how did that strike you, when you first heard Lester? His sound was so different from what was popular or "normal" at that time.
Yeah. Well, his style was sort of new, but we weren't paying too much attention to his style as we did to how he sounded.
He didn't have that rich big sound.

That's right. It wasn't what he played, it was how he played, you see, and Ben actually had the big sound of Coleman Hawkins. Because you must remember then that a reed section was just a tenor and two altos. Then Lester made it sound like three altos. All due respect to Lester Young. Yeah. That was the difference in the sound.
